intro: Look now at the Temple of Apollo at Didyma, built from 300 BC to the 2nd century AD. It was one of the largest temples ever attempted: some 500 years in the building, and never finished. It never had a roof, either. Behind the forest of columns lay an open court, holding the oracle spring and the laurel tree.
spot-1: Now you are looking into the adyton, the unroofed inner court. Here stood the oracle spring and the sacred laurel, open to the sky.
spot-2: Now the camera rests on the naiskos, the small temple inside the court. It housed the bronze cult image of Apollo.
spot-3: Now you are standing in the forest of columns: a double file of Ionic columns, each 19.7 m tall, the tallest in the Greek world. Look up and let their height sink in.
spot-4: Now you are looking at the Medusa frieze, one of the heads that ran round the entablature. A fallen block still lies among the ruins.
spot-5: And beneath it all, the crepidoma: a platform of seven steps, 60 by 120 metres of stone.
uncertainty: Finally, what this model does not know. It shows the temple as designed, not as built: even by the end of antiquity, not all of the columns had been raised. Column diameters, capitals and the height of the entablature are modelled from the proportions of the Ionic order rather than measured, and the carved column bases are simplified.
